newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy backs Albania aid mission, exodus continues.
newsitem.headline: Italy backs Albania aid mission, exodus continues.

text.p: Hundreds more Albanian immigrants arrived in Italy on Tuesday when Rome signalled it was ready to send troops to help a modest humanitarian mission in the chaotic country.

The head of the Brindisi coastguard, Captain Giovanni Biso, said some 500 people disembarked from a merchant ship at the southeastern port in the early hours of Tuesday. The new arrivals brought the flow of Albanians into Italy to more than 12,000 since March 13.
Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Tuesday that Mediterranean countries were in favour of sending troops to the Balkan state as security escorts for aid convoys.

"Certainly Mediterranean countries have already indicated that they intend to participate within the framework of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe," Dini told Reuters before a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Rome.
However Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta indicated that while France would join in, other southern European countries seemed unwilling to commit troops.

"We don't intend to go alone into Albania. Besides the availability of French troops, we are also looking for support to create a European multinational military force," Andreatta said in a radio interview on Tuesday.
He added that military representatives from Spain, Portugal and Greece had "not seemed very interested" by the request for help during talks on Monday.
Dini said Austria and Romania had both signalled a readiness to join a protection force to accompany any aid conveys, while Denmark was also believed to back the plan.
European foreign ministers, meeting in Brussels on Monday, shied away from organising a multinational military force to help restore order in the former communist state.
Dini said the mission could be mounted "before too long" and Andreatta added that any operation would not last beyond June, when Albania is due to hold a general election.
The Italian defence minister was due to meet Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino later on Tuesday to discuss the proposals.
Fino was also scheduled to meet EU foreign ministers, who are in Italy to celebrate the 40th anniversary of the Treaty of Rome, as well as the Pope.
Fino met Italian premier Romano Prodi on Monday, with the two men agreeing to order naval patrols in the Adriatic to stem the exodus of Albanians fleeing armed chaos in their homeland.

The measures, which still have to be fully outlined, followed mounting evidence that recent arrivals were no longer genuine refugees but illegal immigrants looking for a better life, Italian authorities said.
Italian police sources said three of the crew of the Albanian merchant ship which docked early on Tuesday were arrested and charged with aiding and abetting illegal immigration for profit.
Coastguards in Brindisi said radar showed a further 45 boats were sailing in Albanian waters, some of which might be loaded up with immigrants and heading for Italy.
